slides.title: The AI Recommends, a Person Admits
slides.subtitle: Colaberry's AI internship pipeline, read at commit 59720e2
slides.caption: Colaberry's AI internship used to start with an email to two inboxes. This is the pipeline that replaced it.

slides.title: One portal, application to cohort.
slides.subtitle: Consents, interview, decision, documents, payment, membership.
slides.caption: An applicant records their consents, answers one question bank by web form or by an AI phone call, and a reviewer decides. Then come the offer documents, a payment step and a place in the internship cohort.
This is the reviewer's queue. Applicants' names and contact details are hidden in this walkthrough.
The Decide panel puts requirement checks, computed straight from the answers, beside an AI recommendation. The AI never scores or ranks. Only the reviewer can admit.

slides.title: Only a reviewer can admit.
slides.subtitle: No override flag exists in the transition table.
slides.caption: Every step is a transition in one table that names who may take it. Admission belongs to the reviewer alone, and there is no switch that lets the system do it.

slides.title: A model's guess is never an answer.
slides.subtitle: Phone answers wait for the applicant to confirm them.
slides.caption: Answers pulled from a phone interview are stored as needing follow-up, and only the applicant's own confirmation turns them into answers.
Once admitted, each intern is tracked in one console. Unknown is shown as unknown, never as zero, and nudges come from a fixed set of templates.

rows: admission decisions made by a reviewer
AI-flagged applicants the reviewer still approved
slides.caption: On live traffic, all eight admission decisions were made by a reviewer. The reviewer approved two of the three applicants the AI flagged for a closer look, and all forty two signed documents were verified.
Fourteen interns are active with no duplicate memberships. The pipeline was built in ninety four commits over ten weeks.

slides.title: What this record cannot show yet.
slides.subtitle: Whether an intern was hired.
slides.caption: Nothing in the platform records whether an intern was hired, so placement is still unmeasured. The record says so plainly.

slides.title: The AI interviews. A person admits.
slides.subtitle: Built by Ali Muwwakkil, Colaberry
slides.caption: The AI does the work that scales, and a person keeps every admission. That is the part worth copying.
